(1) The binding energy of the 7ΛHe ground state has been determined for the first time using reaction spectroscopy.
the binding energy of 4HeΛ was measured for the first time using a reaction spectroscopy technique.
the binding energy of 6ΛHe has been measured for the first time, and that the binding energy shifts in the A = 6, 7 iso-triplet systems are opposite to those expected from a recent CSB study.

the study of hypernuclei and the search for charge symmetry breaking in ΛN interaction potential.
the search for charge symmetry breaking (and charge independence violation) in the Λ N interaction.
the structure of hypernuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a need for more experimental data, and more detailed theoretical calculations, before a definitive conclusion can be reached regarding the role of charge symmetry breaking effects in the ΛN interaction potential.
the binding energy of 4ΛHe and 4ΛH are not sufficient to determine the sign of the CSB in the ΛN interaction potential.

there is no evidence for CSB in the ΛN interaction potential from the comparison of binding energies of the 4ΛH-4ΛHe system, the 7ΛHe-7ΛBe system and the 5ΛH-5ΛHe system, and that the binding energy differences in the A = 4, 7 and 5 systems are consistent with the predictions of the cluster model calculation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding energy of 4ΛH is 1.01 ± 0.06 MeV.
the binding energy of 4ΛH, the only hypernucleus with a known binding energy, is consistent with the predictions of a simple model that assumes charge symmetry for the ΛN interaction potential.
the binding energy of 4ΛHe is not yet well determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding energy difference of 7ΛBe and 7ΛHe is not a direct measure of CSB.
the binding energies of 7ΛBe and 7ΛHe are not sufficient to test for the CSB in the ΛN interaction.
a measurement of the binding energies of 7ΛLi and 7ΛHe is required to test the validity of the cluster model prediction.
